# `identical-conditional-branches`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports an `if` expression or statement where the `then` and `else` branches
have identical bodies.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

When both branches of a conditional construct execute identical code, the
condition check has no effect on the outcome. This almost always indicates a
copy-paste mistake where the `else` branch was intended to perform different
logic, or dead conditional code that can be removed entirely.

## When it fires

Always. Branches with intentional duplication should include a distinguishing
comment explaining the purpose.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn pick(values: []const u32) u32 {
    if (values.len > 4) {
        return values[0];
    } else {
        return values[0];
    }
}
```
